set.approach: Angel Wings is a backcountry wall in the Sequoia high country, reached from the Crescent Meadow trailhead near Moro Rock on a long walk in. Hamilton Lake is the closest and best camp for the wall. Hell on Wings climbs the south face pillar, following a crack system just left of the Rowell-Jones line.

review.notes: Area page: trailhead and camp. Route page: pillar and line relative to the neighbouring route. Single source for access; no descent source.

Hamilton Lake is the closest and best camp for the wall. The route starts in the middle of the main south face, at the left one of two ramps that cross to form an X a few hundred feet above the base.

review.notes: Area page access; route page start. No descent source.

Hamilton Lake is the closest and best camp for the wall. The Lorax begins from the ramp beside Just a Rock in the Park on its left, then trends leftward past the large roof halfway up the wall.

review.notes: Area page access; route page start. No descent source.

set.approach: Angel Wings is a backcountry wall in the Sequoia high country, reached from the Crescent Meadow trailhead near Moro Rock on a long walk in. Hamilton Lake is the closest and best camp for the wall. This line goes up the left-hand tower of the main wall and finishes at the notch separating it from the middle section.

set.approach: Bat Rock is a small crag on the north side of Highway 155 west of Wofford Heights, reached by a steep hike up from the road. Death March uses a prominent corner with steep, thin cracks toward the right end of the sheer southwest face, then meanders on to the top.

review.notes: Area page: location and steep hike. Route page: line. No descent source.

set.approach: Park at the Pine Creek pack station at the end of Pine Creek Road and walk through the gate onto the Pine Creek Trail. Where the trail forks for Granite Park and Honeymoon Lake, go that way, skirt the lake and climb into the high basin, then leave the trail and camp near Golden Lake. The route is found by looking up from Royce Col.

review.notes: Area page: trailhead and route to camp. Route page: found looking up from Royce Col. Stored grade is aid; the route page describes a scrappy crack line that was nearly freed (grade-type mismatch possible).

set.approach: Walk east from Roads End on the Bubbs Creek trail, the same approach as for Charlotte Dome, to the good campsites just past Charlotte Creek. Continue down the trail a short way until the long wall comes into view on the left. The route follows the longest section of the wall, just left of centre, along a white crystal band. It starts at a big pine just up and right of the huge white left-facing dihedral that marks the foot of that band.
set.descent_text: Parties come off the top by heading west and down the Charlotte Creek drainage, toward Charlotte Dome.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: start and descent. Start and descent rely on the route page alone.

set.approach: Drive Chimney Peak Road to a dirt turnout past the high point of the road, then walk up the ridge northeast of the turnout to Sugar Pine Dome, which is recognisable by the large pine growing at its foot. This flat, waterless spot is the usual base camp, and the other domes are a short walk from it. True Grit is the big roof, climbed from a belay in the crack below it.

review.notes: Area page: approach and basecamp. Route page: roof and belay. No descent source.

set.approach: Hikers take the same way in as for Lone Pine Peak's south face. From where the dirt road above Granite View Drive ends, walk the trail to the Stonehouse, then a use trail up the valley, staying high until the steeper moraine. Follow cairns through the boulder field below the south face of Lone Pine Peak to a flat forested camp with a seasonal stream, near where the south gully enters the canyon. From camp it is a further walk to the foot of the routes, which are on the far east side of the south face.

review.notes: Area page only for access. Route page does not say where on the face it starts; identity vs the area's South Face listing unverified.

set.approach: From the Twin Lakes campground, follow the main trail past the Hulk turn-off to Blarney Lake, where the Peeler Pillar buttress is easy to spot, with the Juggernaut as the other buttress farther south. Continue to Peeler Lake, staying right at the Crown Lake junction, then cut left around the west shore and pick a way over talus to the buttress. Abdication begins at the left edge of the buttress, next to the gully.
set.descent_text: Above the final pitch, a fourth-class ridge leads onto the slopes of Crown Point; either continue over Crown Point's summit or descend to skier's left.

review.notes: Area page: approach. Route page: start and descent (single source).

set.approach: Radiant Dome can be reached from either the Kennedy Meadows or the Manter Meadow side. From Kennedy Meadows, head south along the Kern River on its west bank, cross the Kern and Fish Creek junction, then follow Trout Creek upstream to the east side of the domes. Return to Forever was the first route on the east face and goes straight up from the base on a line of finger to hand cracks.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: line on east face. No descent source.

set.approach: Start from the Paradise Ridge trailhead off Mineral King Road, close to Atwell Mill campground, and hike the trail up to the ridge. Leave the trail there and go cross-country north-northwest, contouring through small drainages until you can see the wall and the gully beneath it. Keep to the gully's east flank until you are below the wall, then cross over and climb to the base. The Siege takes the natural line up the middle of the face on the obvious crack.
set.descent_text: Scramble across to the rear of the formation, rappel into the notch there, and walk the steep dirt and slab around the base of the formation back toward camp.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: line and descent (descent from the route page only).

set.approach: Approach up the North Fork drainage of Lone Pine Peak to Lower Boy Scout Lake. Beyond the lake, a use trail runs toward Mount Carillon's east face; keep the Winged Horse on your left, then cut across to the foot of the wall. The route begins at the centre of the face near a wide pine tree.
set.descent_text: From the summit, rappel once to the west into the gully shared with the Impala. Downclimb the gully, then contour back across to the start of the route.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: start and descent (route page only).
